I posted this because I just saw someone at the store pay 6 bucks for about 4 cups of bland organic brand name chicken broth... For the same price they could have gotten a whole chicken, a half gallon of tasty chicken stock, and had food for 2-3 days. Here is how to do it.

Grab a fat rotiserrie chicken. Pick a freshly cooked one from the back that doesn't have a lot of juice in the tray yet. Bring it home. Pick the chicken, pull off the wings and legs, set aside the breasts, and pick all the little bits off the carcass. Put the bones and skin in a pot with some water, spices, and vegetables, simmer for about 6 hours, and you've got a half gallon of good tasting chicken stock.

  1. Wings for lunch. Eat the legs and wings while they are hot.
  2. Chicken breast sandwiches. Slice one up thin and you can get a couple sandwiches.
  3. Chicken pasta salad - Make some pasta. Add chopped chicken, some vegetables, and oil & vinegar salad dressing.
  4. Rice pilaf with chicken - Make some rice with the chicken broth. Add chicken bits and vegetables and sautee with more broth.
  5. Chicken soup. Take your pick - http://www.cookinglight.com/food/recipe-finder/chicken-soup-recipes/view-all

Stock recipe - http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/alton-brown/chicken-stock-recipe.html

Things to do with the leftover stock - http://www.wisebread.com/25-tasty-ways-to-use-chicken-stock

After all that, take 1 cup of your chicken stock, add 3 cups of water, and you have store bought broth.
How to get 5 meals from a $5 rotisserie chicken
